facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and constipation
continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks
A 40-year-old woman presented with abdominal pain and constipation
continued to have amenorrhea and reported abdominal fullness and constipation
Point-of-care (POC) urine human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) test: negative
Ultrasonography: Confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks

concepts.why: The patient has a high serum hCG level and ultrasonography confirmed a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks.
The patient has a history of thyroid condition, undetectable thyroid-stimulating hormone, and was prescribed methimazole.
The patient presented with constipation and reported abdominal fullness and constipation.
The patient has a tender midline abdominal mass, which could be related to the intrauterine pregnancy.

The initially negative point-of-care urine human chorionic gonadotropin test followed by a significantly elevated serum hCG level is suggestive of a molar pregnancy, which can also explain the abdominal mass and constipation.

rationales.F02: Amenorrhea can be a symptom of intrauterine pregnancy or molar pregnancy.
rationales.F04: Undetectable thyroid-stimulating hormone is a strong indicator of hyperthyroidism.
rationales.F08: A tender midline abdominal mass can be a sign of an abdominal mass or intrauterine pregnancy.
rationales.F09: A negative point-of-care urine hCG test can rule out intrauterine pregnancy or molar pregnancy.
rationales.F10: Elevated serum hCG is a strong indicator of intrauterine pregnancy.
rationales.F11: Ultrasonography confirming a live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks is decisive for intrauterine pregnancy and rules out other conditions.

frontier_selector.rationale: High serum hCG and ultrasonography confirming live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks strongly support this diagnosis, despite initial negative POC urine hCG test.
